evidence.reference_title: Comprehensive genomic analysis of rhabdomyosarcoma reveals a landscape of alterations affecting a common genetic axis in fusion-positive and fusion-negative tumors.
evidence.snippet: In addition to previously reported mutations in NRAS, KRAS, HRAS, FGFR4, PIK3CA, and CTNNB1, we found novel recurrent mutations in FBXW7 and BCOR, providing potential new avenues for therapeutic intervention.

evidence.reference_title: Comprehensive genomic analysis of rhabdomyosarcoma reveals a landscape of alterations affecting a common genetic axis in fusion-positive and fusion-negative tumors.
evidence.snippet: Furthermore, alteration of the receptor tyrosine kinase/RAS/PIK3CA axis affects 93% of cases, providing a framework for genomics-directed therapies that might improve outcomes for patients with rhabdomyosarcoma.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of FGFR4-activating mutations in human rhabdomyosarcomas that promote metastasis in xenotransplanted models.
evidence.snippet: Moreover, 6 FGFR4 tyrosine kinase domain mutations were found among 7 of 94 (7.5%) primary human RMS tumors.

evidence.reference_title: Clinicopathologic and survival correlates of embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma driven by RAS/RAF mutations.
evidence.snippet: Fourteen (54%) cases had NRAS mutations, 6 (23%) had KRAS mutations, 5 (19%) had HRAS mutations, and 1 case (4%) had BRAF mutation.

evidence.reference_title: Anaplastic rhabdomyosarcoma in TP53 germline mutation carriers.
evidence.snippet: In humans, genetic susceptibility to develop RMS has been linked to germline mutations in PTCH1, HRAS, NF1, DICER1, and TP53.

evidence.reference_title: Paternal uniparental disomy with segmental loss of heterozygosity of chromosome 11 are hallmark characteristics of syndromic and sporadic embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Costello syndrome (CS) arises from a typically paternally derived germline mutation in the proto-oncogene HRAS, and is considered a rasopathy. CS results in failure-to-thrive, intellectual disabilities, short stature, coarse facial features, skeletal abnormalities, congenital heart disease, and a predisposition for cancer, most commonly embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma (ERMS).

nodes.description: Loss of imprinting at 11p15 results in biallelic expression of IGF2, leading to autocrine and paracrine growth stimulation through IGF1R signaling. This promotes cell proliferation and survival in ERMS cells.

evidence.reference_title: [Evidence of genetic alterations in chromosome 11 in embryonal and alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma].
evidence.snippet: Allelic losses of 11p15.5 are characteristic of embryonal RMS (eRMS), whereas an increase in the expression of the Igf2 gene located on 11p15.5 has regularly been observed in eRMS and alveolar RMS (aRMS).

nodes.description: Activating mutations in RAS pathway genes (NRAS, KRAS, HRAS) occur in approximately 27% of ERMS cases. FGFR4 kinase-domain mutations were found in 7 of 94 (7.5%) primary rhabdomyosarcoma tumours in the study that first reported them - note that denominator is rhabdomyosarcoma overall rather than ERMS specifically. These mutations drive proliferation through MAPK and PI3K pathway activation.
